title: One member per email
statement: Two members MUST NOT share an email address. Emails are compared without regard to case or surrounding spaces.

title: A member holds at most 3 active loans
statement: A member MUST NOT hold more than 3 active loans at once. A loan stops counting when it is returned.

title: A member with an overdue loan cannot borrow
statement: A member who has an overdue loan (see TL-LEND-DR08) MUST NOT start a new loan until every overdue loan is returned. There is no grace period and no librarian override.

title: A tool's condition is good or needs repair
statement: A tool's condition MUST be either `good` or `needs_repair`. A new tool starts as `good`. The same two values are used when a return records a condition.

title: A tool that needs repair cannot be lent
statement: A tool whose condition is `needs_repair` MUST NOT be lent. It returns to lending only when a librarian marks it repaired.

title: A tool is lent to one member at a time
statement: A tool MUST NOT have more than one active loan. It can be lent again once its loan is returned.

title: A loan is due 14 calendar days after it starts
statement:
A loan's due date MUST be the date it starts plus 14 calendar days, both dates taken in the library's time zone. The due date is a date (YYYY-MM-DD), not a time: it is stored and shown that way. The loan is due by the end of that day.

The library's time zone is a setting, an IANA name, defaulting to `America/New_York`. For example, a loan started at 23:30 on 2 March in New York (04:30 on 3 March in UTC) is due on 16 March.

title: A loan is overdue from the day after its due date
statement: A loan is overdue when it has not been returned and today's date, in the library's time zone, is later than its due date. A loan is never overdue during its due date, up to and including 23:59 that day in the library's time zone, even when UTC has already moved to the next day. It becomes overdue at 00:00 on the next day in the library's time zone. A returned loan is never overdue.

title: A loan is returned once
statement: A loan MUST be returned at most once. Once returned, its return time and condition MUST NOT change.

title: A return records the tool's condition
statement: Every return MUST record the tool's condition as found by the librarian, the time of return, and MAY record a note.

title: A good return does not clear damage reported during the loan
statement: When damage is reported on a tool while it is on loan, a return that records the condition as `good` MUST NOT clear that damage. The tool stays `needs_repair`, with its damage note, until a librarian marks it repaired.
